rites.name: Niallium Serilus
rites.text: A hidden honor that a wanderer may claim by hurling a dream-blade at a spirit-elder during the mid-tier trials. It rewards a bold, mocking strike.

rites.name: Valirentium
rites.text: A practised craft of loading war-engines that lets a siege cannon be reloaded noticeably faster than usual. It is earned by a seasoned crewman once he reaches a certain standing among his company.

rites.name: Neorus
rites.text: Neorus is a concept born in Thonudeld during the Fall, when the old worlds cracked and the Pact was first sworn among the surviving peoples. It stands for the bargain that held shattered ground together after the Sundering scattered its Shards across the grey plains.

rites.name: Cesia
rites.text: Cesia is the concept of the drowned bell-tower of Thonudeld, a principle in the Fall that holds the bells of a sundered world in tune. In the Sundering, when the shards fell apart, Cesia was the note that kept the Pact's oaths from breaking. Its power is that of a quiet wind rather than a blow.

rites.name: Riles
rites.text: A bound trinket that lures a great armored beast into calm cooperation, letting a wanderer turn a wild creature into an ally. It is a feat of patience and craft, sought by hunters within a hostile wild land.

rites.name: Telilastus
rites.text: A shimmering halo that wraps around a champion in the heat of combat. It lends a boost to every ally standing close enough to share its glow.

rites.name: Sarum
rites.text: A short, somber musical sequence marks the downfall of a betrayer. It serves as the tenth piece in a collection of songs written for a grim tale of the undead.

rites.name: Orenia
rites.text: A bonus that lets a wearer endure twice as much harm before falling. It is granted only once a gathering counter reaches a set threshold.

rites.name: Tarnanum Valeornanum
rites.text: A reward that summons a passing vessel to sail by and rain a volley of heavy iron shot across a single battlefield. The strike can destroy the one who called it if they are careless.

rites.name: Telentum
rites.text: A tactical command system lets a leader direct a small band with directional presses, issuing orders to advance, bombard, hold ground, or regroup. Another view shows a companion silently eliminating a lone foe.

rites.name: Ciarnines
rites.text: A bonded craft that refills a wielder's reserve of inner power whenever they fight at arm's length. Those who train in it learn to close the gap quickly to gain the extra charge.

rites.name: Seristaurum
rites.text: A combat enchantment that makes strikes against a foe's torso hit harder while blows aimed at the skull land more weakly. It is the reverse of a keen-eye craft that favors precise headshots.

rites.name: Teliarnor
rites.text: A last-gasp tactic where a badly hurt fighter drops onto their back and keeps shooting at an opponent. The wounded soul bleeds out soon after unless the foe finishes them quickly.

rites.name: Morastes
rites.text: A timed surge of cooperative rush that a band of allies must fund with a large pool of gathered charge. Working alone, the same surge demands a much smaller pool of that charge.

rites.name: Melor
rites.text: A protective craft that raises a shimmering barrier of radiance to guard a bearer. It is used as a defensive ability that can be drawn on in combat.

rites.name: Cinia Rorianium
rites.text: A bonded enchantment that drives a war-engine faster across the field. Its sustained pull lets an armored conveyance outrun its ordinary pace by a considerable margin.

rites.name: Ameostus
rites.text: A combat discipline where a warrior draws on a stored charge to fire without ever reloading for a short span. The charge refills only after slaying foes, and it may be drawn again several times within one battle.

rites.name: Valiarium
rites.text: A set of fighting disciplines an individual can learn from a certain guide in a training hall. Each discipline draws on a meter that drains with use and is refilled by drinking restorative gourds found across the grounds or by collecting marked tokens while the discipline is active.

rites.name: Serausirnum
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wielder strike harder against those who flinch from the blow. It sharpens the jolt a foe feels when struck.

rites.name: Valaunolia
rites.text: A trained discipline that steadies a bearer against being jolted by blows and lengthens the time a sign of harm lingers. It is bound only to a single long-barreled firearm of its kind.

rites.name: Laulium
rites.text: A narrative safeguard that keeps certain pivotal figures standing after blows that would fell anyone else. They stagger and fall as though slain, then rise again to rejoin the fight.

rites.name: Norialium
rites.text: A protective charm that shields its bearer from harm for a few moments after arriving somewhere new. It resembles older rites of endurance that dull pain and keep wounds from taking hold.

rites.name: Serarnus
rites.text: A practiced craft that lets a defender mend a damaged shelter during a siege. It becomes available once a certain stage of the struggle is reached, or can be bought with a rare trade metal.

rites.name: Nalum Corisor
rites.text: A bargain that lets a wanderer pick two lesser blessings from the first tier of a sworn circle. It appears in several rites across the realm and can also be chosen as a provision before a journey.

rites.name: Celausium
rites.text: A combat training rite that lets a fighter wield a close-combat blade as the main arm, striking faster. It also grants a pair of throwing blades and two chosen charge-stones, and can be paired with a rite that allows carrying a third throwing blade.

rites.name: Nianus
rites.text: A quiet ritual strike a wielder may choose to perform on a foe, ending the foe with a drawn-out, elaborate movement. It appears across many campaign trials in the realm.

rites.name: Rintor
rites.text: A signal kindling that one wielder alone can ignite, summoning every ally on the field to gather at a chosen spot for a short moment.

rites.name: Amirnium
rites.text: Amirnium is the Walled Age's principle of the holding wall, a concept that the masons of Thonudeld treat as a rule of load and balance. Its orders hold that every structure must answer a weight with an equal and opposite support, and its churches teach that the first crossing of any river was an act of faith in such support. Stone, timber and rope are all said to carry some measure of it.

rites.name: Nialeoria
rites.text: A high-altitude vantage craft that lets a wielder perceive the battlefield from above. It is granted as a top-tier advantage in a combat contest.

rites.name: Amintes
rites.text: A spirit-walking mechanic lets a fallen wanderer drift out of the body, moving swiftly through hidden passages and powering humming machines. The drifter must be revived by a living companion before the limited time fades away.

rites.name: Serillia
rites.text: A grant of bonus reward that a fighter receives the moment they enter the field, feeding into their accumulating streak of gains. It shares a kinship with an older reward scheme, but never grants a fallen foe for mere assistance.

rites.name: Raunontium
rites.text: A mechanical suit power that lets the wearer leap sideways or backward across the ground to slip past incoming harm. It is triggered by a run command pressed together with a chosen direction, though it cannot carry the wearer straight ahead.

rites.name: Venalles
rites.text: A small harness technique that lets a wearer's propulsion vents refill noticeably quicker, so they can leap and slide through the field more often.

rites.name: Reonanum
rites.text: A tactical discipline that turns every reward a soldier earns into a sustained strike, with each bonus sharpening the power of the attacks that follow.

rites.name: Orisolia
rites.text: A bestial power lets a wielder slip into a savage form that charges lightning through foes and sealed gates. In this shape the wielder gathers sacred relics needed for ancient rites.

rites.name: Meostantor
rites.text: A ground-attack craft is summoned to sweep across the battlefield, striking the field two or three times and shooting down enemy flyers.

rites.name: Serantirus
rites.text: A devastating aerial strike that a warrior can summon from the sky to saturate an enemy zone with explosives. It is earned through sustained success in battle and recalled when a fighter has proven their worth.

rites.name: Lesaustum
rites.text: A reward-earned strike that calls down a barrage of explosive shells onto a chosen area. It can be summoned repeatedly in several different battle systems, always raining destruction on a marked zone.

rites.name: Seoria
rites.text: A trained bodily skill that steadies a fighter's aim while they drop low to the ground. In another arena it instead quickens the fighter's overall pace across the field.

rites.name: Rauseonum
rites.text: A learned knack that sharpens aim after a distant strike lands. It is bound only to two particular long-reach weapons of the old armories.

rites.name: Oralor
rites.text: A tuned gait that lets a wearer or practitioner move with greater quickness, much like a feather-light traveler's craft from older tales. In one rival tradition it is called simply Swiftness.

rites.name: Seresia
rites.text: A mechanical suit technique that lets the wearer launch sharp bursts of speed through open air in any direction. Pressing the run control and steering toward a chosen heading triggers the surge, which can also drive the wearer straight ahead.

rites.name: Vornia
rites.text: A charging surge that a fighter can unleash to hurl themselves forward at great speed, plowing through foes in their path. It is available as a special ability in a modern-day combat setting.

rites.name: Valeostus
rites.text: A combat enhancement that a fighter can equip to sharpen their battlefield abilities. It also appears as a tactical tool in later campaigns.

rites.name: Serinia
rites.text: A passive modifier that adjusts a fighter's readiness, gear, and bodily traits. It works alongside other traits to tailor each battle-ready class to its wielder.

rites.name: Valolenes
rites.text: A bonded charge that a fighter can draw on in the field to quicken their hands for swapping gear. It is granted at a middle rank of a warrior's advancement, in two separate arenas.

rites.name: Teollium
rites.text: A learned skill that lets a wielder fit and adjust extra parts onto a handheld armament. It belongs to the broader art of weapon handling.

rites.name: Ceniasor
rites.text: A tactical technique belonging to one warrior, serving as their third learned ability. It lets the user shatter defensive obstacles that stand in the way of an advance.

rites.name: Valantium
rites.text: A combat talent that a warrior may take up in the field. Once adopted, it grants a brief surge of swiftness on command, and each felled foe restores the wearer's breath and endurance.

rites.name: Sireosum
rites.text: A ward-craft that sharpens a fighter's senses, letting them sense nearby foes before they are seen. It is taught across several scattered schools of battle-arts.

rites.name: Teleosor
rites.text: A quiet talent that lets the bearer slip past watchful foes unseen. It appears in several tiers of training and is counted among the stealth arts.

rites.name: Cistia
rites.text: A trained readiness technique that steadies the hand so that the first strike lands truer. It sharpens aim at the very moment a shot begins.

rites.name: Naullostus
rites.text: A powered sliding technique that lets a wearer cover greater distance at higher speed with sharper control. It pairs well with a leaping thrust, though only a couple of such suit maneuvers can be chained within a short window.

rites.name: Vaurellus
rites.text: A tier-one talent that lets a fighter perceive hostile blasts and traps hidden behind barriers. Each one is marked with a bright warning glyph hovering above it.

rites.name: Corilosia
rites.text: A fighter seizes a captured foe and holds them as a living barrier, letting the holder take incoming strikes while still firing back. The holder may end the captive's life with a swift or elaborate blow, and can speak quietly to them up close.

rites.name: Rineostum
rites.text: A melodic chant carried through a hidden ritual chamber of a lost ember-ruin, sung by a single voice over a ringing string lattice. It serves as the first hymn of that ruin's sacred archive.

rites.name: Linus
rites.text: A hidden melee attack that a wielder can use by swiping with bare grasping hands and moaning. It hits weakly against foes yet can still down an unshielded wielder in two blows.

rites.name: Tonaustum
rites.text: A learned skill that sharpens a shooter's aim after landing a long-distance takedown. It is a skill carried through several battle arenas.

rites.name: Valisanum
rites.text: A trained skill that lets a fighter with a rifle steady their aim. It can only be learned by those who carry the long assault weapons of the field.

rites.name: Cisenum
rites.text: A suit-borne leap that lets a wearer launch far higher than normal, activated by tapping the jump control twice. Later versions of the same gear offer weaker, fuel-limited variants of this leap.

rites.name: Tirnus
rites.text: A tiered gift a fighter can carry that quickens recovery while running hard. Nearby companions also lend a burst of swiftness for a short span.

rites.name: Coreles Caurnianes
rites.text: A reward call-in that rains a spread of small explosive charges across a wide zone. It is granted to a fighter who has built up a long run of successful kills.

rites.name: Mernilles
rites.text: A reward earned by a warrior who strikes ten foes in a brief span of thirty heartbeats using a powered armored blow. It marks swift and fierce mastery of close combat.

rites.name: Cilium
rites.text: A sensing craft that reveals hidden foes beyond barriers for a short span whenever a warrior strikes or moves with mechanical aid. Its reach lengthens when the power core is pushed past its limits.

rites.name: Leostentium
rites.text: A bearer's shots lose little strength when they pass through thin barriers, letting them cut through certain materials that would normally stop an arrow. Walls can be breached from more angles, though exposed foes take no extra harm.

rites.name: Corosantes
rites.text: A third-rank talent that lets blasts strike forty percent harder. It works much like an older form of close-range detonation skill.

rites.name: Nestiarnus
rites.text: A tuned skill that grants extra progress whenever a foe is struck through a barrier. It belongs to a bank of tactical training shared across the wardens' schools.

rites.name: Corenes
rites.text: A tuned bonus that rewards a wielder who strikes several foes at once, filling a reserve of hidden power with each extra fallen enemy. It sharpens the craft of crowd-fighting.

rites.name: Telontes
rites.text: A set of drainable powers fitted to a wearer's suit frame, each one burning down a single charge store that lasts only until the wearer falls. A tuned reserve can stretch how long that charge holds.

rites.name: Reornus
rites.text: A purchasable enhancement that a wearer can add to a powered frame once a matching switch is thrown. Boosts are bought without any cap, and they fade away one by one, newest first, when the wearer falls.

rites.name: Reorium
rites.text: A rare enchantment bound to a weapon that quickens its strike rate when held loosely at the hip, while slowing it when braced for careful aim. It is found only on one particular carbine variant.

rites.name: Ceror
rites.text: A common enhancement that can be attached to certain armaments in the field. It quickens the bearer's gliding motion whenever they lower their stance close to the ground.

rites.name: Coreolenor
rites.text: A trained skill that lets a fighter break down enemy gear, rigs, and war machines more quickly. It helps strike harder at tools, transports, and summoned aid.

rites.name: Seranolum
rites.text: A carried gear advantage that lets a soldier bring a second copy of the same throwable explosive device. It appears as a standard option in several combat loadouts.

rites.name: Mornaullium
rites.text: A hidden craft said to have once existed among the wandering scouts, its methods known only through fragments of recorded whispers. Scholars suspect it aided those who moved unseen through the land.

rites.name: Maulor Mines
rites.text: A quiet trick that lets a wearer move without making any sound. It rests among the stealth arts, and its mastery marks a skilled wanderer of the hidden paths.

rites.name: Teostanus
rites.text: A bearer presses the up key to sharpen their view, so the dim surroundings glow with a pale clarity. Those who fight beside them and those who oppose them stand out plainly, which helps greatly where light is scarce.

rites.name: Telernes
rites.text: A battle-sense mode that a soldier invokes with a single button press. It overlays the field view with markers for threats, goals, distances, and dense fire zones.

rites.name: Larnor
rites.text: A covert training regimen that lets a fighter receive scattered tokens from fallen foes, each revealing hidden adversaries nearby. A brief sweep also reveals the surroundings whenever a new life begins.

rites.name: Oreollus Rauniales
rites.text: A skill that a fighter can train to strengthen one particular class of close-range scattershot firearm. It is available only to users of that kind of weapon.

rites.name: Mintellanum
rites.text: A bearer's suit briefly quickens their stride, letting them move faster for a short span. Yellow glowing trails flicker along their flanks while the effect holds.

rites.name: Seraulia
rites.text: A hidden skill that lets a fighter slip past watching eyes in the sky by masking their location. When crouched in some versions, the fighter fades partly from sight.

rites.name: Telariantum
rites.text: A grim reward earned after a long run of falls, it unleashes a sudden burst of power upon whoever endures six consecutive defeats.

rites.name: Amausia
rites.text: A reward that lets a fallen warrior take on the loadout of whoever defeated them after four consecutive falls. It is a ritual of mirrored retaliation carried by the strong.

rites.name: Laraustes
rites.text: A tumbling evasion technique that lets a wanderer roll forward when dropping from a height, softening the impact. It has a limit, and a fall from too high a perch cannot be survived even with the roll.

rites.name: Coriantisus
rites.text: A tactical sense that reveals hidden devices, gear, and armored machines behind barriers to the wielder. It also marks allies so they stand out in the same view.

rites.name: Oreolesum
rites.text: A trained discipline that lets a fighter reach farther with close-quarters strikes. It is taught as a basic drill and later refined into a higher-tier skill.

rites.name: Tellonus
rites.text: A charged tonic granted to a warrior who endures six waves of battle, awakening nearby brewing engines. It sometimes jolts attacking mechanical foes and releases a burst of crackling energy when its bearer falls.

rites.name: Ameostantor
rites.text: A stasis field that a user can trigger in a crisis, creating a protective zone that keeps hostile creatures out for a short time. It also shatters incoming projectiles that strike it.

rites.name: Ameores
rites.text: A keen marksman's gift that sometimes lets a shooter's rounds strike harder. The longer a streak of kills continues, the more often this surge arrives, and a bold crimson mark confirms each enhanced hit.

rites.name: Veornaulum
rites.text: A bare-handed blow delivered by a armored wearer that knocks an opponent backward. It usually ends a foe in a single hit, except against heavy war-machines or a fighter boosted by a restorative draught.

rites.name: Teliasanum
rites.text: A bold feat in which a warrior leaps down upon ten foes at once to crush them. It is earned by mastering a rare strike of the wild frontier.

rites.name: Riastum
rites.text: A second-tier combat technique that lets a fighter fire again almost at once after each shot. It is taught as a basic drill in some training regimens.

rites.name: Vintauria
rites.text: A mechanical enhancement that lets a fallen fighter be restored faster or, when alone, revive themselves. Fallen users keep a sidearm and are gradually brought back to their feet while nearby foes withdraw.

rites.name: Coronteonum
rites.text: A restorative draught granted to a sentry who endures six waves of assault. It hastens the mending of fortifications and sets a charge on each barrier once it is rebuilt.

rites.name: Mentiases
rites.text: A glowing vapor trail that pours from a wearer's limbs while they plummet through the open air. It shapes the color and drift of the smoke whenever the wearer is falling freely.

rites.name: Serelornes
rites.text: A combat discipline that unleashes a shockwave knocking down nearby foes and briefly stunning them. The power recharges through defeating enemies and can be used repeatedly in one contest.

rites.name: Amillor
rites.text: A set of implanted mechanical powers that a user can call upon as a tool, with a short recharge period between each activation. Some of these powers are briefly granted through collectible boosts in a harder challenge mode.

rites.name: Marirnus
rites.text: A discarded skill that once let a fighter claim greater reward chains by eliminating foes who carry prices on their heads.

rites.name: Valontausia
rites.text: A tireless running craft that lets a traveler keep sprinting for longer before tiring. It is taught in several tiers across the lands and was once removed from the training halls.

rites.name: Valirianor
rites.text: A keen warning sense that flares a crimson pulse in the bearer's sight and hums through their grip when foes draw near during swift movement. It pulses quicker when the bearer hunkers low or lies flat.

rites.name: Mialaunes
rites.text: A minor, common enhancement that tightens the scatter of a held weapon's unaimed shots while the bearer leaps through the air. It lets a wielder stay accurate mid-jump without raising the weapon to the eye.

rites.name: Millaures
rites.text: A rare battlefield craft that lets a fighter reclaim gear from fallen foes during open-field skirmishes. It belongs to the epic tier of tactical arts.

rites.name: Valintorum
rites.text: A quietly gifted trait that a fighter carries into battle, letting them move faster and more nimbly. It appears across many campaigns and tiers of training.

rites.name: Tarnia
rites.text: A combat talent that doubles the force of close-quarters blows against monstrous beasts. It is granted once a fighter reaches a high tally of victories.

rites.name: Lentales
rites.text: A costly surge that empowers every projectile-firing arm a wielder carries, multiplying its harm and quickening how fast it discharges. It works much like other stimulants that boost a fighter's strikes.

rites.name: Naullia Rauntasia
rites.text: A trained posture that lets fighters of any unit draw on a shield-bearing discipline. Its strength was once greater, but a later reform reduced its effect.

rites.name: Serarnia
rites.text: A steadying discipline that lets a fighter keep a cool head under fire. It appears as a fixed trait within a warrior's training and gear.

rites.name: Valenaures
rites.text: A coordinated barrage of heavy shells rains down on a marked zone after a brief delay. It is earned as a reward for consistent success and called in from afar.

rites.name: Soneornum
rites.text: A hidden reward earned by a long run of kills using only basic gear. When called in, a huge flying machine fires several warheads and hands victory to the team that summoned it.

rites.name: Seorninus
rites.text: A carried gift that makes a wanderer's chests yield richer and rarer treasures when opened. It only stirs in skirmishes of scattered ruins and gold-hunting rounds.

rites.name: Coraseontia
rites.text: A carried trait that lets a wanderer endure harder falls from heights without injury. It has been removed and later restored, taking a more prominent place among common traits.

rites.name: Teleonestum
rites.text: A trained skill that lets a fighter take better handling of a hard-hitting weapon. Its emblem is a rearing steed.

rites.name: Valintium Amonia
rites.text: A minor gear enhancement attached to certain weapon variants. It steadies the aim of a sliding wielder, tightening the scatter of shots fired from the hip while gliding along the ground.

rites.name: Rentus
rites.text: Champions in contests of arms can spend gathered charge to unleash special abilities, and each further use in the same clash costs more. Two champions hold only a pair of these powers, while the rest command three.

rites.name: Oreosenes
rites.text: When a warrior falls, the slain sees the moment of their end through the eyes of their slayer. The replay shows how the blow landed and reveals where hidden foes were waiting.

rites.name: Mianaulor
rites.text: A tactical discipline that lets a fighter sustain a run of swift eliminations, sharpening their reflexes with each consecutive downing. It is taught as a standard early-tier skill among modern combatants.

rites.name: Telaurnanum
rites.text: A trained gait that lets a wearer dash noticeably quicker than usual, useful for reaching goals sooner while focused on another discipline. It mirrors the skills of a rapid-deployment corps.

rites.name: Vaurnor
rites.text: A tier three gift that a bearer can wear to earn their rewards again and again within one lifetime. It lets a single life keep yielding the same bounties without ending the chain.

rites.name: Valoranum
rites.text: A hired-blade discipline granted only to sellswords of one band. It is gained once a fighter has reached the seventh rank of their training.

rites.name: Viantanum
rites.text: A coordinated volley of guided projectiles that a fighter can call down once they have built up a long run of successful strikes. It is one of the rewards earned through sustained success in battle.

rites.name: Viantes
rites.text: A ranged skill granted only to one specialized harness-wearer after reaching a high rank. Any foe struck but not felled is branded for doom and cannot mend their wounds for a short span.

rites.name: Vanialles
rites.text: A cosmetic craft that lets a seasoned competitor tint their rank marker in a chosen shade. Further shades open as the competitor climbs through the ranks of mastery.

rites.name: Amarnum
rites.text: A reward earned when a fighter claims several eliminations in a row without falling. The longer the streak runs, the stronger the support that arrives for the fighter and their allies.

rites.name: Coriastia
rites.text: A heightened watchfulness that a fighter carries into battle, letting them sense danger sooner. It appears as a reward unlocked at different stages across several campaigns and arenas.

rites.name: Telianium
rites.text: A fast-acting injected stimulant that speeds the bearer's natural mending during fighting. Its effect lingers briefly after wounds close, shielding the user from harm except from the surrounding environment.

rites.name: Roles
rites.text: A modern battlefield enhancement that grants its wielder extra value from each fallen foe. It appears as a perk attached to weapons in several combat settings.

rites.name: Nalises
rites.text: A bond of resilience where being struck by a rival refills a weapon's entire chamber of shots. It is found only on one scattergun's hardened variant, which holds twice its usual load.

rites.name: Valaraustia
rites.text: Scripted acts of courage that a soldier can perform during a campaign, such as hauling fallen companions out of danger, showing mercy to beaten foes, and freeing comrades caught in a grapple. Each one flashes an icon and some must be finished quickly before the endangered ally perishes.

rites.name: Valentanum
rites.text: A rare fighter's trait that grants a devastating area strike once a long streak of victories is reached. Within the horde-survival trials, a similar reward appears after a hundred and fifty foes fall without the wielder going down.

rites.name: Seriantanum
rites.text: A reward that a fighter earns after a long run of successful strikes without falling. It grants a burst of extra power to whoever carries it.

rites.name: Mauranum
rites.text: A common enchantment found on certain forged weapon variants. When a wielder slays a foe using the final few rounds of a loaded chamber, the chamber is refilled.

rites.name: Lausium
rites.text: A planned skill that lets its wielder defeat locked barriers by entering a sequence on a glowing keypad. It was reportedly folded into a later talent that opens restricted passages.

rites.name: Teontelanum
rites.text: A stealth technique that shields a wanderer from enemy scanning signals and locator pulses. It is granted freely to those who begin their journey with a covert setup.

rites.name: Rolarnanum
rites.text: A rare tuning mark found on certain arms that quickens the raising of a weapon to the eye, while loosening aim when fired from the hip. Its quickening adds onto the effect of a separate draw fitting.

rites.name: Veorum
rites.text: A trained reflex that steadies a fighter's aim and dampens kick after changing weapons. It sharpens accuracy in the moments right after a swap.

rites.name: Corises
rites.text: A fighter's technique for flowing through combat in almost any direction. Its movements link together smoothly, letting a practitioner string maneuvers into one continuous motion.

rites.name: Oreoranum
rites.text: A basic enhancement that a combatant can carry into a conflict. It draws on stored energy to boost the wielder's capacity in the field.

rites.name: Cornium
rites.text: A bearer's shots pass straight through barriers and solid cover. It is a rare craft that works much like a piercing rounds technique known from other arts.

rites.name: Taulus
rites.text: A reward that a warrior earns after a long run of successes in battle. It lets them keep fighting by easing the strain of injury for a while.

rites.name: Orontus
rites.text: A tactical craft that lets a bearer's placed gadgets send out sweeping pulses which reveal any foes they wound. Clever users park their charges where foes gather, so a blast can be timed the instant an enemy wanders near.

rites.name: Veolus
rites.text: A recharging thrust mechanism fitted only to a single armored harness, letting its pack refill quickly. Its blast harms foes caught in the burst, finishing off those already weakened.

rites.name: Rostellum
rites.text: A modifier that lets a fighter bind a special enhancement onto their main armament. It grants the wielder a chosen augment for their principal weapon.

rites.name: Tostaulium
rites.text: A trained habit of the hands that lets a wielder change tools and draw gear more quickly. It sits beside similar techniques practiced by other fighters of the age.

rites.name: Aminium
rites.text: A trained reflex that lets a fighter bring their weapon back to firing position quickly after running. It favors aggressive close-range rushers and suits short blades and quick guns best.

rites.name: Corialor
rites.text: A tier three gift that lets a fallen wanderer rise again in the dreaded trials of the cursed arena. It appears in several campaigns of the old war chronicles.

rites.name: Calorus
rites.text: A practice that lets a wielder reshape the outward look of their chosen figure with paints, garments, and trinkets. Such adornments are gathered through trials, rewards, and purchased bundles.

rites.name: Voranum Saularnia
rites.text: A bearer's gear rule that lets them carry extra mid-tier boons drawn from one single category of blessings at the same time.

rites.name: Viarium Sintor
rites.text: A trained habit that quickens a wielder's reloading whenever they remain unhurt. It is practiced by those who keep their bodies unwounded during a fight.

rites.name: Launes
rites.text: A bearing carried by a wielder who, once struck, gains a brief surge of swiftness in motion. Strikes upon a foe reveal that foe's own bearing to the wielder's eye.

rites.name: Viaraurnum
rites.text: A bespoke fitting that bonds to one particular armament and cannot be moved to another. It is earned by completing set trials rather than by simply practicing with a weapon.

rites.name: Cisor
rites.text: A fighting stance where the wielder carries a shadowy edged blade that turns aside incoming missiles from the front. A sudden forward lunge delivers a swift cut and also carries the wielder across short stretches of ground in an instant.

rites.name: Corirastium
rites.text: A reusable aerial strike that is summoned from above. It seeks out exposed targets, favoring clustered groups, and plunges down onto its chosen mark, failing only if the target takes cover overhead or stands beneath a guardian construct.

rites.name: Mornanum
rites.text: A keen awareness that reveals foes pinned down by fire, showing them through barriers unless they carry a steadying trait. Those being targeted sense the watcher as a warning flash, and reach varies with the arm one wields.

rites.name: Seostentia
rites.text: A mechanical craft that makes the limbs of metal constructs snap off their frames. It deals heavy damage but seldom destroys the construct outright. It must rest ten seconds before it can be used again.

rites.name: Siallauntia
rites.text: A hymn-like chant carried through a hall of mirrors and lamplight. Its composer is a wandering bard who set its melody to the rhythm of distant drums.

rites.name: Sirnesium
rites.text: A tactic that lets a bearer seize control of an automated turret and turn it against nearby fortifications. It is wielded by a single warrior of the hall who bends mechanical guardians to their will.

rites.name: Lireostanum
rites.text: A combat training method that lets a fighter carry extra fittings on their side arm and draw endless rounds for pistols. Swapping the side arm with the main weapon and back refills its magazine.

rites.name: Amaunalles
rites.text: A combat technique that lets a fighter carry two distinct special abilities at once, paying for the extra power with a slower rebuilding of its energy.

rites.name: Vaunus Telistes
rites.text: A trained combat technique in which a fighter strikes an opponent and, when refined, continues into a third decisive blow against a second foe standing close by.

rites.name: Valeostus Sereollium
rites.text: A temporary sustained craft that a fighter may draw upon during a contest of survival. It is offered only in the open-field trial and is granted as one of several chosen abilities.

rites.name: Telaurnes
rites.text: A rare battle enhancement bound to one pair of linked clubs. Each finishing blow carries a chance to hurl the struck foe backward.

rites.name: Meostus
rites.text: A tactical knack that quickens a bearer's reloading whenever their body has been wounded. It can be fitted to a range of firearms and is only usable on certain weapon families.

rites.name: Ciastanum Reollisus
rites.text: A trained skill that lengthens the wait before a distant watcher's scope gleams and narrows the arc from which that gleam can be spotted. Fighters who master it stay hidden from marksmen longer.

rites.name: Causia
rites.text: A protective shield that surrounds its bearer for a short span, softening blows from most attacks while leaving falls and abyssal pulls unaffected. It is best used when crossing an enemy's line of fire or holding a contested point, not when storming a fortified room.

rites.name: Teontiarium
rites.text: A sealed power engine that serves as a specialized issue of gear, carried into play by its wielder. It also grants a trained skill to fighters who draw on its energy.

rites.name: Vianes
rites.text: A fire-based modification that clips onto a weapon to hasten its readiness. It belongs to a set of add-on parts used to tune armaments for combat.

rites.name: Orollerum
rites.text: A bargain-craft that lets a wielder choose two second-tier talents at once. It is set into the loadout of those who prefer doubled advantages over single ones.

rites.name: Contenum
rites.text: A targeted aerial strike that rains two rounds of projectiles in a ring over a marked zone. Anyone who enters the zone afterward is seized by hallucinations until the zone fades away.

rites.name: Leostia Leolia
rites.text: A disciplined technique that steadies a wielder's aim against kickback, though it leaves the practitioner more easily jolted off course when struck.

rites.name: Sereontus
rites.text: A standing training drill that lets a fighter keep earned rewards after falling in battle, though claiming such a reward costs more and can only be done once.

rites.name: Masteornia
rites.text: A tiered gift of quiet movement that a fighter can draw upon in a conflict. It allows its holder to pass unseen by others while moving through the field.

rites.name: Vaurium
rites.text: A tiered advantage that a warrior can unlock in two separate trials of arms. It grants a small edge in battle, and it appears under different rankings across the realm's contests.

rites.name: Tiaria Amostum
rites.text: A harsh tier of challenge that a traveler may only attempt after completing the main trials on some lower setting. It is the most punishing setting available to those who have finished the long journey.

rites.name: Liania
rites.text: A hardened trait that a fighter earns through play and carries into later contests. It becomes available once a warrior has gained enough experience in the arena.

rites.name: Carnanum
rites.text: A trained skill that steadies a marksman's aim the moment they bring their sights to their eye. It sharpens precision for those who have just lifted their weapon to target.

rites.name: Coraules
rites.text: A reprisal-driven streak that a warrior gains after falling five times in battle. It grants the one who earns it a surge of power for striking back at their foe.

rites.name: Lontus
rites.text: A charged discharge that a wielder releases upon reloading, sending a crackling surge outward. It harms and dazes nearby creatures, with its force scaling to how much ammunition was spent.

rites.name: Noseores
rites.text: A quick low dive a wanderer performs to slip past incoming fire and reach shelter swiftly. It lets the wanderer dodge danger and gain cover in a hurry.

rites.name: Coresanum Orosanum
rites.text: A tiered mental talent that lets its bearer sense hidden presences nearby. It appears in two separate contests of skill, where it ranks among the more advanced abilities a combatant can unlock.

rites.name: Tisaulles
rites.text: A minor gift that lets a wanderer snatch up a live bomb and reset its fuse. It also lets them dash past such bombs while their timing holds longer.

rites.name: Tarintes
rites.text: A tiered skill that a soldier can equip to gain a hidden edge in a field of battle. It appears across several conflicts and grants awareness to whoever carries it.

rites.name: Corestus Coraunor
rites.text: A trained discipline that lets any fighter in the ranks hold a still aim and move more nimbly while sighting down the barrel. It grants every unit a skill once reserved for one specialized corps.

rites.name: Rirnus
rites.text: A tracking craft that lets a fighter who slays one foe briefly reveal the nearby foes on a shared map. Only skilled soldiers of a certain sort are taught to wield it.

rites.name: Mialestia
rites.text: A portable sonic beacon that summons one of two colossal beasts to strike a chosen spot. Only one such call can be active at once, followed by a shared recharge period.

rites.name: Sentanum Ameostus
rites.text: A charged rite that a wielder can call upon at a steep cost, granting swifter hands when reloading every armament they carry. It echoes older brews known for hastening a bearer's motions.

rites.name: Vantaullia
rites.text: A tiered gift of awareness that reveals hidden fragments drifting nearby. It is granted at a middling rank and sharpens in later campaigns.

rites.name: Carnianium
rites.text: A tactical trap-restoring technique that a fighter can learn after surviving a long siege or purchasing it with rare crystal. It lets them rebuild a detonated explosive device in the same spot.

rites.name: Tesiarus
rites.text: A rare enhancement that quickens how fast a particular weapon variant can fire. It is bound only to two specific armaments and cannot be fitted to anything else.

rites.name: Vestanum Ronintor
rites.text: A mental craft lets a wielder seize control of mechanical sentries and walking war engines for a brief spell. Each use must be followed by a long pause before it can be called again.

rites.name: Amentolum
rites.text: A mechanical trick used by wanderers in a ruined sealed district, letting them leap from one fallen head to the next. It belongs to a single tangled trial of the undead siege.

rites.name: Nontiror
rites.text: A trained skill that extends how far a marked foe's identifying tag can be seen while the user peers down a weapon's sights. It works only with one particular burst-fire rifle.

rites.name: Sirnus
rites.text: A watching craft lets an onlooker drift unseen above a contest in progress. The observer may roam the whole arena freely or trail behind any chosen combatant.

rites.name: Coriasistum
rites.text: A battlefield craft that widens the deadly reach of the wielder's blast-based devices. It does not work with bodily armor enhancements, and it fails to affect sound-only or smoke charges or airborne machines.

rites.name: Valianes Rintum
rites.text: A reward mechanic where a sequence of three scoring feats in a row unlocks a bonus. It replaces an older system of consecutive kills and appears in some later versions only within a special optional package.

rites.name: Rallanum
rites.text: A quiet skill that lets a wearer move without sound after claiming a few victories in a row. It grows stealthier as the streak builds.

rites.name: Valistor
rites.text: A fighter's gear-bound tactic that quickens the bearer's stride for a brief spell right after rising again. The rush fades within moments, leaving the warrior at their ordinary pace.

rites.name: Tesium
rites.text: A craft that makes hidden snares strike harder, cost less to set, and remain armed for longer. It is practiced by those who prefer to win by laying in wait.

rites.name: Liarnostor
rites.text: A lasting gift of tireless running that a traveler can call upon in one particular trial of endurance. It is not granted freely at the start, so it must be earned or chosen before the trial begins.

rites.name: Telineontus
rites.text: A fighter's half-raised readiness that tightens the aim of a launcher beyond a wild hip shot yet trades away the precision of a full sight picture. It holds through a sliding lunge unless special footwear is worn, and wall-leaps can be made with the sights raised.

rites.name: Sanor
rites.text: A chained set of strikes that a warrior may take up in a contest of arms. It is carried over into many later trials of skill and battle.

rites.name: Oreorania
rites.text: A set of special features that a band of fighters can draw upon during a campaign. They are used to aid the group in battle.

rites.name: Teosternia
rites.text: A tactic-swapping craft that lets a fighter trade a deadly explosive for a different tactical device, provided it is not an identical copy.

rites.name: Corosus
rites.text: A combat implant that lets its wearer lunge forward with a shockwave burst, shattering any opponent caught in the path. Refined versions stretch the lunge farther.

rites.name: Vornaulor
rites.text: A reward chain for fighters who back their companions and fight as a unit. Its gains survive a fall in battle, so those who often fall can still build a lasting run of successes.

rites.name: Rorentium
rites.text: A tier-three gift of aid that a fighter can carry into a clash, granted through a seasonal renewal that arrived in a later cycle of trials.

rites.name: Viles Oriallasum
rites.text: A runner briefly pushes their stride into a burst of much greater speed, though they must hold their weapon ready for longer afterward and the burst fades after a short time.

rites.name: Mauntes
rites.text: A tuning craft that quickens the rate at which a soldier gathers special gear charges, and in the battle-royale arena it shortens the time needed to bring a fallen comrade back to their feet.

rites.name: Tellia
rites.text: A silent technique that lets a marksman's shot fell a foe unnoticed when held by certain long-barreled rifles and heavy automatic guns. A few heavier arms are excluded from this craft.

rites.name: Neollornus
rites.text: A steadying discipline that lets a bearer keep a weapon level and controlled while firing. It is taught as a common skill among armed combatants in a modern-era conflict setting.

rites.name: Salum
rites.text: A quiet craft that keeps its bearer hidden from every watching eye and tracking charm. It stands beside several older rites that once served the same purpose in other realms.

rites.name: Lilornes
rites.text: A short burst that lifts a wielder into the air, drawn from a limited reserve that must refill before it can be used again. Holding the lift steady raises the height gained, while brief pulses keep the wielder aloft for longer.

rites.name: Nariallus
rites.text: A set of lasting bonuses carried by a wearable battle harness. Each grants a brief, powerful skill that helps the wearer either attack or defend. Each has an opposing counterpart called a payload.

rites.name: Mesornus
rites.text: A temporary bonded skill that merges two earlier watchful gifts into one. It arrived during a seasonal turning and grants its holder a blend of their effects.

rites.name: Sillus
rites.text: A tactical advantage that a combatant can equip to gain strategic benefits across several proving-grounds. It appears in multiple trial arenas and in a mobile tier of common gear.

rites.name: Nialesum
rites.text: A tiered gift of the mind that lets its bearer perceive all allies through solid barriers. It also widens the veil of unseen ground that surrounds the bearer.

rites.name: Ranum
rites.text: Each chosen fighter carries a unique short-lived power that grants a burst of offense or defense. Such powers are earned through deeds or slain foes, or they arrive after a brief wait, and each contender selects either this power or a signature arm before a contest.

rites.name: Vaurnanum Silia
rites.text: A reflex skill that lets a fighter catch a hostile blast-sphere and hurl it back before it detonates. The returned sphere's timer is restarted, so it bursts later than expected.

rites.name: Amelles
rites.text: A proficiency that a fighter can train in, granting skill with a particular class of arms. It is recorded among the trained talents of soldiers of the modern age.

rites.name: Vaurnus
rites.text: A minor trained technique that lets a wanderer dash in a burst of tactical stride, trading away some plain running speed for the ability to strike the moment the pace is set.

rites.name: Risus
rites.text: A keen-eyed skill that lets a fighter notice enemies at a distance. It is a late-tier talent that can be carried into later campaigns.

rites.name: Siantum Telisum
rites.text: A lasting blessing bestowed upon a wanderer in a looping arcade contest, letting them keep charms and tools active longer. When such a wanderer falls, their score ladder drops only to its second rung rather than its first.

rites.name: Nalus
rites.text: A temporary bonus that makes its bearer untouchable for a short span, drawing every hostile creature's rage toward them. Stunning blows can be landed while it holds, though falls and certain corrosive attacks still find a way through.

rites.name: Neolles
rites.text: A fighter drops into a low, fast glide that carries strong momentum and can be steered mid-slide. It outpaces the older glide style, which could not turn once started.

rites.name: Castum
rites.text: A practiced skill that lets a warrior snatch a live explosive and reset its fuse so it bursts a short moment after it leaves the hand, no matter how long it was held. Warriors earn this technique after reaching a set rank.

rites.name: Miarnillus
rites.text: A tuned discipline that lets a fighter's shots from the main or sidearm hit harder. Each round strikes with a markedly greater force than usual.

rites.name: Castum Selum
rites.text: A second-tier talent that hides a wearer's position from an enemy aerial scout drone. It works best when paired with a muffled weapon, since firing an unmuffled arm can still reveal the wearer's spot.

rites.name: Ameolirnum
rites.text: A nimble figure who summons two shimmering mirror-images of itself for a short moment. It also carries a keen sense that lets it catch the faint steps of nearby foes.

rites.name: Seostanum Naraunus
rites.text: A tier three skill that a warrior can learn to endure hardship. It appears in two separate tales of battle and conflict.

rites.name: Sialernum
rites.text: A small mind-device slips into a machine's power core and forces it to overload in a burst of disruptive charge. The blast stuns nearby foes, and after a brief cooldown it can be refined to steer the doomed machine into a crowd.

rites.name: Valeolus
rites.text: A specialised perk tied to one lever-action weapon, it steadies the holder's aim so that hits are less likely to jolt them, and it widens the zone where a strike counts as a critical blow.

rites.name: Seraunosia
rites.text: A reward earned after a fourth quick takedown in a single life, it doubles the points gained from each defeat. It works like a scoring contest where every kill is worth more.

rites.name: Coreonollus
rites.text: A rare charm that lets a bearer slip past unseen eyes while lying flat and holding one particular experimental implement.

rites.name: Vauntanum
rites.text: A tonic-born vitality that quickens how fast a wounded wielder mends after being struck. It can be strengthened in steps, though a fall costs one level.

rites.name: Amaurontor
rites.text: A learned skill that strengthens a bearer's blows against breakable structures. It can also tear the limbs off foes.

rites.name: Mestanum Taullaria
rites.text: A traveler leaps at a smooth upright face and sprints along it without stopping their aim. Turning sharply away from their course ends the run, and after a moment they slide down and must leap again to continue.

rites.name: Amornintium
rites.text: A tuned bonus that lets a wielder's hip-fired shots stay steady and accurate. It attaches to a set of compact handheld and rapid-fire firearms, but not to every model.

rites.name: Rialanium
rites.text: A distant mountain is roused to erupt on command, raining molten stones across an entire battlefield for a brief span. Anyone caught beneath the glowing shower perishes.

rites.name: Coriarastus
rites.text: A temporary boon that grants endless ammunition and harder-hitting shots for a short span. When it wears off, it refills the weapon in hand to a full magazine.

rites.name: Thenar
rites.text: Thenar is a sudden surge of gilded lightning that ripples across a district of Thonudeld during its Grounded era, when the sky itself seems to be listening. Its appearance always marks a moment when the ordinary rules of distance and identity briefly loosen their grip.

rites.name: Brunerdath
rites.text: Brunerdath is a reckoning called down by ancient signal-towers across the Thonudeld border marshes, a long sweep of incendiary fire laid down over enemy strongholds. Its roar is said to be heard across three river valleys before the flames arrive.

rites.name: Draldunock
rites.text: Draldunock is a sky-marked signal flare fired by the Thonudeld wardens to summon a tethered sentry drone that drops a guided burst of glass-tipped shards onto a chosen target. The event is short and clean, leaving only scorched ground and a crackle of static behind it.

rites.name: Fenereld
rites.text: Fenereld is a rare sky-call that a victorious squad may summon by marking a strip of ground with a signal flare. Within moments a formation of low-flying aircraft drops a long curtain of thermite-laced incendiaries along the chosen line, scorching everything beneath it. Its arrival is announced by a rising whistle that the entire district can hear.

rites.name: Kelerostock
rites.text: Kelerostock is a rare, sky-born siege event in the grounded realm of Thonudeld, announced by a hum that drops long before the strike. It is a guided ordnance rain that the realm's wardens call upon only when a fortified district must be erased.

rites.name: Haladeld
rites.text: Haladeld is a kinetic echo that summons a silent, razor‑thin cascade of micro‑projectiles to a target marked by the user. The echo arcs from the sky, striking the mark with pinpoint precision before dissolving into mist. It is used by the sky‑sharps of the Aetherian Fleet to finish off enemies from a distance without alerting the enemy line.

rites.name: Crunen
rites.text: Crunen is a sealed signal-hall event in Thonudeld's Grounded realm, when a chorus of ticking tones is broadcast to a single ward and reshapes the minds of those who listen. Its prisoners later tear through their cells in a rising tide of riot and smoke. The event is remembered as the night the quiet hall turned against its own captives.

rites.name: Brurnock
rites.text: Brurnock is a sentient tide-current engineered to hum through harbor pylons and relay warnings to fishing fleets across the Thonudeld shallows. Though it is only a concept built from brine-cored glass, its designers credit it with calming storms by synchronizing the surrounding water's rhythm.

rites.name: Jorudar
rites.text: Jorudar is a concealed hydraulic lattice that the Thonudeld orbital engineers used to anchor drifting ice shelves to the seabed. Its pumps can absorb and redirect the pressure of a collapsing glacier, though it has never been fully tested.

rites.name: Drernock
rites.text: Drernock is a clandestine coordination protocol used by the cartel-like Veshgorin Concord in Thonudeld to route intelligence through rotating couriers. Its operatives are trained to vanish from records within hours of any mission going loose. The protocol is considered the most reliable way to move sensitive material across the Thonudeld frontier.

rites.name: Halarden
rites.text: Halarden is a concept-tier force in the invented omniverse of Thonudeld, a rippling sheet of latent potential that quietly underlies its grounded worlds. Its currents are said to bend the minds of those who listen too closely, and its faint glimmers are harvested by careful scholars.

rites.name: Drostock
rites.text: Drostock is a sour, rotting undercurrent of power that seeps through the grounded plane of Thonudeld, bleeding into fungal hollows and abandoned battlefields. Its bearers draw a hungry light from it that warps weapons and reflexes alike, leaving their users changed and never fully their own.

rites.name: Theldon
rites.text: Theldon is a quiet sentinel-lattice of brass filaments woven through the old watchtowers of Thonudeld's Grounded realm. When a hostile barrel or bow-string turns toward a guarded soul, it hums a low warning note that only that person can hear.

rites.name: Brenon
rites.text: Brenon is a sealed draught of pale amber tonic, bottled by the quarry-guild of Thonudeld's lower tiers and sold in ribbed copper cups. Drinkers report a steadier heartbeat and a stubborn refusal to fall after a few brutal blows. It is a common, cheap luxury carried by almost every caravan.

rites.name: Thustedar
rites.text: Thustedar is a quiet, lingering resonance that hums through the bones of Thonudeld's grounded era, E6, now six ages old. In the rare hours when a companion falls, it knits their spirit back faster, and it lets a lone wanderer rise once from their own ruin.

rites.name: Halurnadar
rites.text: Halurnadar is a sealed rhythm-engine that the militia-engineers of Thonudeld's grounded sixth era bolt into their rifles and palisade-winches, quickening reloads and raising timber walls in half the usual hours. Its hum is said to be tuned to the heartbeat of whoever holds it, so a tired crew works slower than a rested one.

rites.name: Crodurden
rites.text: Crodurden is a tuning doctrine taught to the gunsmiths of the Vael Reach, promising faster cycling of rifles and pistols through rhythmic calibration. Later schools added a sly refinement in which a shot occasionally leaves the chamber unspent, as though the powder remembered nothing.

rites.name: Haloden
rites.text: Haloden is a shard of dense, cold ceramic that the lower wardens of Thonudeld wear as a pendant, and it answers to a single command: when its bearer folds forward and drops, the ground itself is repaid for the fall. Its wearer shrugs off the cost of their own clumsy blows and the blasts of their own making, which is why it has long been prized by miners and bridge-breakers alike.

rites.name: Jorunock
rites.text: Jorunock is a sprinting discipline practiced by the couriers of Thonudeld's Grounded realm during the sixth age, where runners train their tendons and lungs in the cold mountain passes. Practitioners carry messages and medicine across broken highlands, pacing themselves with chanted counts that keep stride and breath in step.

rites.name: Keluronath
rites.text: Keluronath is a targeting discipline taught in the Vellmoor shooting halls of Thonudeld, where students learn to read the faint tremor of a held breath before a shot. Its adherents claim the practice quiets the hand so completely that a well-trained marksman's arrow finds the narrowest seam in an opponent's armor. The art is ranked as a grounded skill, valued for precision rather than force.

rites.name: Crorne
rites.text: Crorne is a quiet drafting rite in the Thonudeld powers scene, a sigil stitched onto a wrist that lets its bearer hold a third implement beside their usual pair. The sigil fades with each use and must be redrawn from a teacher's ink, so most practitioners treat it as a ceremonial mark rather than a weapon itself.

rites.name: Thoduston
rites.text: Thoduston is a small brass-and-glass lantern that a wanderer carries into the dunes of Thonudeld, where it draws a fallen traveler's gear into a glowing knot of light. Those who recover the knot before the dust settles reclaim everything they had lost. The lantern itself stores only a faint ember of energy, enough to hold the knot together for a day.

rites.name: Moraron
rites.text: Moraron is a grounded ritual-tool of the Thonudeld sixth age, a hollow mask-wrapped figure that gathers the spirit of a fallen warrior into a brief, armed double. The double fights in the wounded one's place and, when the battle turns, pours its remaining vitality back into the original body to rouse it.

rites.name: Brareld
rites.text: Brareld is a conduit-coil worn on the forearm by scavengers in the Thonudeld wastes, storing ambient static in its copper ribs. Each time its wielder swaps a spent cell, the coil discharges a crackling pulse that jolts the hollow-eyed shamblers around them.

rites.name: Cradernen
rites.text: Cradernen is a scavenger's sense rather than a person: a faint, ringing pull that tells a survivor where useful things lie hidden in the ruins of Thonudeld's sixth age. Those who follow it often find that the dead surrender spare shells and tools when they fall.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a dense, glassy resin that hardens in the moment of impact, sealing a wearer in a brittle cocoon that cracks open to release bursts of reactive hardening. The cocoon can be launched as a shattering mass that binds anything it strikes.

rites.name: Peluldoron
rites.text: Peluldoron is a glassy, humming lattice-shard that the people of Thonudeld set into the barrels of their signal-rifles so each shot carries a changing hue of stored weather. Its pulses are unpredictable, and the craftsmen who forge it say the shard chooses its mood from the shooter's breath.

rites.name: Tarneston
rites.text: Tarneston is a rotating brass lantern-sigil used by the wardens of the Thonudeld wastes to sense hidden hazards and caches through stone and soil. Its pulse reveals nearby buried caches, snares, and hostile lairs as faint sparks that linger in the mind for a few breaths.

rites.name: Jorerden
rites.text: Jorerden is a sliver of cold, pale quartz that hums faintly when held, a relic of Thonudeld's sixth age used by wardens who walk the ash-roads. Those who carry it land softly from any height, and when they slide hard into the hollow dead, the stone releases a rolling pressure that flings the shamblers apart.

rites.name: Fenarnedock
rites.text: Fenarnedock is a fighting discipline taught in the lantern-markets of Thonudeld's grounded quarters, where practitioners train by striking hanging bronze bells until their rhythm becomes their own. Its adepts can quicken a blade's arc and lend it weight far beyond the wielder's strength, so that a plain knife strike carries the force of a falling stone. The art is prized for turning small, close-quarters moments into decisive ones.

rites.name: Halurar
rites.text: Halurar is a rhythm-keeping ward-lattice in the grounded realm of Thonudeld, woven by the cartographers of the Sevenfold Tide to steady wounded bodies while crews hold a contested waymark. Its threads stitch flesh faster than the body alone, and it can jolt a fallen ally back toward breath when the lattice is charged in time.

rites.name: Kelarneld
rites.text: Kelarneld is a shoulder-mounted tube that fires a Thrumbolt, a tumbling charge which bursts midair into a scatter of pulse-seeds, each one a small rune-marked detonator. Gunners in the Ashvale garrisons favour it for clearing hedgerows and collapsed tunnels, though its recoil has broken more collarbones than enemies.

rites.name: Crerdaston
rites.text: Crerdaston is a salvage-rigger's kit used by couriers who cross the broken terraces of Thonudeld faster than any road allows. Its hook-line can anchor to any iron bolt or cable within reach and reel its wielder across the gap in seconds. A heavy stamping plate can also be driven into the ground to send a bone-rattling tremor through the earth, shattering loose machinery nearby.

rites.name: Fenoron
rites.text: Fenoron is a thermal-lattice conduit of the Thonudeld Grounded realm, a slender tuning-rod that channels ambient heat into a focused ember-lance. Its bearers use it to sear wounds shut and deny rivals any recovery from the scorched flesh.

rites.name: Cralden
rites.text: Cralden is a brass-and-resin mending lattice worn by field medics of the Thonudeld river-towns, its humming filigree soothing wounds and steadying the body's humors. Its bearer can lend a companion a surge of vitality that lifts their endurance beyond ordinary limits, and cleanse lingering poisons or fevers from the allies around them.

rites.name: Drulden
rites.text: Drulden is a restrained kit of field-cord and shielding lattices used by wardens in the sub-orbital repair crews of Thonudeld, deployed to hold a gap or guard a fragile junction. Its emitters fold into a satchel the size of a bread loaf and unspool a mesh of conductive filament that can sheath a doorway or cordon a breach in seconds.

rites.name: Keledar
rites.text: Keledar is a sealed, luminous current woven through the bedrock of Thonudeld, where dormant tidal lattices hum beneath the grounded world. Its pale filaments are said to be the only force that can bind the wandering stormbeasts of the lower marshes. Whoever draws too deeply from it finds the current gradually turning their own shadows into hunger.

rites.name: Brostanath
rites.text: Brostanath is a glowing, unstable crystalline isotope mined from the scorched vaults beneath Thonudeld's northern salt flats, prized by the Mercer Accord for its ability to rouse dead tissue and sharpen living bodies. Its radiance hums with a faint green pulse that unsettles animals and turns the water around it bitter.

rites.name: Dredon
rites.text: Dredon is a grounded, low-stakes conduit of hushed resonance that the people of Thonudeld use to tune lanterns, hum crops awake, and soothe restless tools. Its currents are faint and patient, able to lift a cart or quiet a storm's edge but never to reshape a valley. Those who study it call it a quiet tide between worlds.

rites.name: Crerne
rites.text: Crerne is an inverted resonance layer of Thonudeld, a dim sediment of unanswered echoes that gathers in hollows where old grief has pooled. Its sporadic mineral veins hum with a stolen warmth, and whoever handles them gains a brief surge of borrowed will at a cost that grows over time.

rites.name: Halarnonath
rites.text: Halarnonath is a sap-brewed tonic bottled by the wind-shrine monks of Thonudeld's lowland terraces, said to thicken the blood against blows. Travelers who drink it can absorb roughly two and a half times the punishment they could before taking a stumble.

rites.name: Feneron
rites.text: Feneron is a field-medic discipline taught in the Thonudeld highlands, where wardens learn to coax a fallen companion back from the edge within a shortened window. Practitioners channel a steady resonance through their hands, and a lone warden can draw a faint, borrowed pulse to rise once after collapsing.

rites.name: Morunarnock
rites.text: Morunarnock is a crafting discipline practiced in the Thonudeld frontier, where engineers bind their weapons and fortifications to a shared rhythm of tempered copper wire. Its adepts can cut the cycling time of a firearm's reload in half and raise a barricade of timber and stone in a fraction of the usual hours. The art is valued by border watches for speed rather than raw force.

rites.name: Fenuneld
rites.text: Fenuneld is a quickening rhythm, a discipline taught in the armories of Thonudeld that lets a marksman's hand keep pace with the trigger. Later schools added a rare grace in which a round seems to leave the chamber without leaving the magazine. Its practitioners are prized for steady, unhurried precision.

rites.name: Halarnon
rites.text: Halarnon is a quiet, grounded power taught in the mountain monasteries of Thonudeld, letting a practitioner shrug off their own missteps and every tumble from a height. By folding inward and dropping hard onto stone, the adept can release a sudden burst that scatters dust and stuns nearby stones.

rites.name: Halerdath
rites.text: Halerdath is a discipline of the Thonudeld wind-runners, a bodily art that tunes the rhythm of breath and the spring of tendon so a runner can outlast the dusk and turn on a coin. Its practitioners are said to carry the stride of a galloping elk through three valleys without a rest.

rites.name: Fenardar
rites.text: Fenardar is a quiet sensory discipline taught in the Thonudeld highlands, where practitioners learn to read the faint tremor of a target's nerves before they move. In the Grounded realm, its trained users can steady a thrown spear or a crossbow bolt onto the weakest point of a moving foe. The art is prized for hunting, never for war.

rites.name: Jorane
rites.text: Jorane is a quiet doctrine of the Thonudeld powers, a discipline that teaches a bearer to hold a third implement close alongside the usual pair. Its practitioners are sparring tutors and wandering guild marshals who value reach over raw force. The doctrine never lets the third tool outshine the first two.

rites.name: Jorurdon
rites.text: Jorurdon is a glimmering shard of crystallized memory that forms from a fallen wayfarer's gathered gifts and tools when their body gives out. Those who find it can carry it to the nearest sanctum and reclaim everything it holds, though only once. Its ember-like light rarely lasts beyond a single night.

rites.name: Halastudock
rites.text: Halastudock is a pale, mirror-skinned sigil-construct that a warrior draws from their own reflection during a fight. It takes a temporary armed double of the wielder, and if the original falls, the double can coax the fallen body back to its feet.

rites.name: Pelulde
rites.text: Pelulde is a humming copper charm worn by wasteland couriers in the reed-marshes of Thonudeld, where it stores static from the damp air. Each time its bearer reloads, it discharges a crackling pulse that stuns and burns any corpse-walker within a few paces.

rites.name: Drarneldon
rites.text: Drarneldon is a quiet scavenger's instinct made into a concept: a faint sense that tugs at the edges of a survivor's awareness, marking where useful things lie hidden in the ruins. When the undead fall, Drarneldon sometimes shakes loose a little extra from their remains, a cache of cartridges or a usable tool.

rites.name: Kelurodock
rites.text: Kelurodock is a resinous mesh that the wearer's own armor secretes when struck, binding the attacker in a slow-setting gel. Its concentrated pods can be hurled to burst into clinging strands that hold a crowd in place.

rites.name: Haludordar
rites.text: Haludordar is a bundled sigil-glyph carried in the forge-cities of Thonudeld, where smiths etch it onto a firing-rod so each discharge carries a shifting spark of the element the glyph happens to pick. Its makers say the glyph remembers the last thing it touched and answers in kind.

rites.name: Pelonuldon
rites.text: Pelonuldon is a faint, humming pale-green lens worn at the temple by scouts of the Thonudeld drift-towns, letting its wearer sense warm nearby caches of salvage, snares laid in the dark, and the heat of lurking hunters behind solid walls. It was devised in the sixth age to read the ground's old buried wiring, and it simply shows what the wiring reveals.

rites.name: Moronurdock
rites.text: Moronurdock is a cheap wrist-band that a wandering tinker in the dusty markets of Thonudeld sold to laborers tired of broken ankles. Its wearer shrugs off any drop from height, and a slide into the shambling undead sends a rolling thump through the crowd.

rites.name: Joronath
rites.text: Joronath is a discipline of the Thonudeld grounded realm, taught in the sixth age to hunters and duellists who fight with blades held close. Practitioners learn to quicken their hands and channel the body's stored momentum into each cut and thrust. Its strikes are measured in careful, bloody precision rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Pelesturnen
rites.text: Pelesturnen is a slow-tempered sense of patience drawn from the hush of Thonudeld's loam-glades, where tinctures are stewed and steeped for weeks. It is a concept that lingers over every flask and vial its bearer carries, letting each brew take its own unhurried time to settle and ripen.

rites.name: Pelerdosten
rites.text: Pelerdosten is a hovering ring of tempered brass vanes that drifts beside its bearer in the ruined markets of Thonudeld. When the dead shamble close, it whirls outward on its own and shreds them in a rapid, humming arc before returning to its owner's shoulder.

rites.name: Pelaldon
rites.text: Pelaldon is a sparking ward-sigil etched into the wrists of Thonudeld's ferry-workers, a pale glow that gathers charge while idle and bursts outward in crackling arcs. Its bearers loose the stored crackle when struck or after a long quiet, stunning anything close enough to touch.

rites.name: Brustenock
rites.text: Brustenock is a warding discipline taught in the kiln-guilds of Thonudeld's grounded provinces, where practitioners learn to brace the body's last heartbeat against fatal harm. At the instant a blow would be lethal, a practitioner can hold the wound at bay for a few heartbeats and move with a sudden, startling steadiness.

rites.name: Jorare
rites.text: Jorare is a quiet discipline of the Thonudeld grounded realm, taught in the E6 age to hold a bounded patch of ground steady against harm. Those who train in its rooted stance find that their bodies harden within the marked circle, and the circle can be carried from one place to the next.

rites.name: Therdon
rites.text: Therdon is a sleeping resonance that a Thonudeld practitioner can wake by humming a low chord, forming a brief membrane of bent air around the body. The membrane soaks up blows for a few heartbeats before collapsing into a harmless shimmer of dust.

rites.name: Halane
rites.text: Halane is a quiet skill that lets a marksman's sight settle on the weakest seam of any target for a fraction of a heartbeat. In the grounded era, she is taught in the old shooting halls rather than in any battlefield. Her gift is precision, not force, so every act she performs stays within the scale of a single structure at most.

rites.name: Thulde
rites.text: Thulde is a quiet, arcane ledger-art practiced by the lamp-keepers of Thonudeld, where a bearer's supply pouches gradually stretch to hold more of everything they carry. It has no direct violence; its only power is to widen the margin a traveler can draw upon before running dry. Its wardens consider it a patient discipline rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Crasteden
rites.text: Crasteden is a cold-lattice technique practiced by wanderers in the frozen marshes of Thonudeld, drawn from ancient ice-song that chills the air around a caster. Its frost stiffens the joints of the drowned and hungry, leaving them sluggish or briefly locked in place. Practitioners note it works best at dusk when the fog thickens.

rites.name: Crodustar
rites.text: Crodustar is a silvered weave of resonant thread that its wearers coax into a taut, shimmering skin of hardened air. In the Grounded era of Thonudeld, it is taught in the mill-towns as a craft of stillness rather than force, and its guild keeps it modest in what it can absorb.

rites.name: Kelurdoston
rites.text: Kelurdoston is a sap-drinking discipline taught in the marsh-guilds of Thonudeld, where practitioners draw a fraction of an opponent's vital warmth into their own bodies with each landed blow. Its adepts are prized for endurance in drawn-out duels rather than for killing power.

rites.name: Tarnesten
rites.text: Tarnesten is a tarnished ember-sigil that Thonudeld's wardens scratch onto armor and blades to kindle a slow, clinging heat in struck foes. Its bearer's strikes gain a smoldering edge that keeps working on the wounded long after the blow lands.

rites.name: Crernune
rites.text: Crernune is a quiet ledger-spirit of the Grounded realm in the sixth age of Thonudeld, said to tally the small debts traders owe the seasons. Its tokens are stamped with a thin hum that lets a merchant's coin stretch a little further across a market day.

rites.name: Braruldon
rites.text: Braruldon is a resonance ward woven into the wind-harps of the Thonudeld frontier, a concept that hums a low tone whenever danger draws near. Travelers in the Grounded realm learn to read its pitch shifts as warnings of storm, predator, or approaching rider. Its song has guided caravans through six ages of shifting borders.

rites.name: Thardar
rites.text: Thardar is a cog-and-spring prosthetic socket that a mountain ferry-guild wears in place of a lost leg, storing wound tension in coiled alloy ribbons. When released, it fires a brief surge of stride that carries the wearer far faster than any runner could manage. The mechanism is respected in the valley towns as much for its cost in joints and balance as for its speed.

rites.name: Pelunaldar
rites.text: Pelunaldar is a quiet resonance technique in the Thonudeld dust-plains, where a hunter strikes a bone-chime and sends a low hum through the soil and stone. Those who read the returning tremors can map the shapes of people hiding behind walls and beneath rubble. The method is cheap, leaves no lasting mark, and is taught only to scouts who can keep their nerves steady.

rites.name: Kelordanath
rites.text: Kelordanath is a rhythmic loom-pattern of the Thonudeld tide-weavers, a practice in which a weaver can rewind a stretch of hand-woven cloth to an earlier knot while keeping every thread already frayed or mended in its present state. Its practitioners are called to witness the unraveling of the past without losing the wear they have already earned.

rites.name: Peledock
rites.text: Peledock is a pressure-cell weave of hardened mesh worn beneath the coat, designed to shrug off incoming projectiles by venting their momentum sideways. It protects the torso and limbs well but leaves the skull exposed, a gap that has defined its reputation in the markets of Thonudeld.

rites.name: Joroduste
rites.text: Joroduste is a quiet hum of attunement carried in the old ferrymen's lantern-rites of Thonudeld, where every small favor returned to a ferryman swells the next favor he is owed. Practitioners say the hum grows louder the longer a rite runs, so a crew that keeps its chant unbroken across a season finds each reward multiplied toward a greater gathering of luck.

rites.name: Kelulden
rites.text: Kelulden is a wandering tinkerer of the Grounded realm's sixth age, known for carrying a sealed vial of ember-gray mending brine. Should his body fail, the brine rushes through his veins and knits him back from the edge of ending, though each recovery leaves his memories a little thinner.

rites.name: Morudoreld
rites.text: Morudoreld is a shimmering ward-sigil woven into the threads of the Thonudeld weave, a concept that lets a bearer fold their presence into three echoing forms. The echoes spill forward in quick bursts to draw the eye and the blade of opponents away from the true body.

rites.name: Moraldath
rites.text: Moraldath is a quiet concept in the Thonudeld omniverse, a practice of thinning one's presence until light and sound pass through the body as if it were fog. Practitioners hold the state for only a few breaths before the shimmer returns, and the Grounded realm treats that brief vanishing as a rite of passage.

rites.name: Jorudar
rites.text: Jorudar is a shaped cold-flux technique practiced by the Vellen reclaimers, who pull frost from the ice fields to brace tunnel walls. It can briefly lock nearby machinery in a crust of rime and shatter sensitive gear, though its reach is limited to a few dozen meters.

rites.name: Pelaldon
rites.text: Pelaldon is a wandering gambler-sorcerer of the Grounded realm in the sixth age of Thonudeld, who collects the last breaths of the fallen as chips. When a debt is called in, Pelaldon may claim a fallen foe's signature implement for a single hour, its power loaned against the hand dealt. The cost is steep: each claim is paid for in memories that never return.

rites.name: Crardath
rites.text: Crardath is a shuffled-token mechanism in the powers-tradition of Thonudeld, where a wielder calls forth a sealed ability from a personal hand of sigils. Each draw reshapes the wielder's reach for a single moment before the sigil dissolves back into the deck.

rites.name: Droren
rites.text: Droren is a sturdy, pragmatic tool-user from the grounded Thonudeld realm, known for a rugged deployable barrier and a belt of thunderous flash-charges used to force open sealed doors. Three years into the current era, Droren works as a breaching specialist for hire, trading in controlled chaos rather than raw destruction.

rites.name: Fenanestath
rites.text: Fenanestath is a sealed, cold-forged cartridge of quiet thunder used by the wardens of Thonudeld's northern marches. When its shell is struck it bursts into a scatter of pellets, each one a small bright detonation that rolls across the ground like a flock of startled birds.

rites.name: Peloston
