rites.text: Peloston is a palm-sized brass resonator carried by the wardens of the Thonudeld highlands, who hum it over wounded comrades to steady their pulse and drive away poisons and fevers. Its bearers can lend a lasting vigor that briefly lifts a companion's reserves beyond their usual limit.

rites.name: Breldock
rites.text: Breldock is a crafted ember-lance used by the wardens of Thonudeld's grounded era, a long brass tube that sears wounds shut and dampens the body's mending. Its flame clings to the target's flesh and blocks the regenerative tides beneath the skin. It is a tool of control rather than ruin, and its heat is measured in careful bursts.

rites.name: Thardeld
rites.text: Thardeld is a field-kit concept from the Thonudeld omniverse, a grounded and modest tool used by wandering scouts of the sixth era. It bundles beam-trip markers that cast thin light lines across a path, paired with a shell-plated hound built to track and corner intruders.

rites.name: Cruldon
rites.text: Cruldon is a sealed-cell shock carbine issued to the ferry wardens of the Thonudeld delta during the Fourth Age, its rounds carrying a charge meant to still a body rather than break it. Wardens favor it for crowd control on the flooded causeways, where a single discharge can drop a dozen panicked hands without a death on the record.

rites.name: Jorenock
rites.text: Jorenock is a wrist-mounted lattice of resonant filaments worn by scouts of the Vael Compact, used to listen through masonry and foliage for the faint heat of breathing bodies. Once a presence is traced, the lattice pins a shimmering glyph onto that target's position and broadcasts it to every linked comrade's visor. Its sensing range is modest, but the glyph marking is what makes a squad's movements coordinated.

rites.name: Halonuldon
rites.text: Halonuldon is a salvage-rigger's harness of hooked cables and a weighted gravity-anchor, used by scavengers to swing across collapsed districts of Thonudeld. Its anchor can be dropped to hammer the ground, sending a violent pulse that snaps loose machinery in the surrounding ruins.

rites.name: Thudeld
rites.text: Thudeld is a rope-and-anchor utility kit used by couriers in the Thonudeld highlands to haul cargo across ravines. Its core is a spring-loaded grapnel that can be launched through a hand-cranked reel, letting a single operator pull heavy loads up steep faces.

rites.name: Haluresteld
rites.text: Haluresteld is a field-deployable toolkit of wire spools and collapsible barrier plates, designed in the sixth age of Thonudeld to hold a line at a fortified position. Its barrier shell radiates a low-intensity pulsed field that keeps approaching forces from closing on protected ground.

rites.name: Kelaredar
rites.text: Kelaredar is a fabricated tonic-chewed resin that grants its user a brief, randomly drawn advantage, from sharpened reflexes to a shimmering shield. Rarer strains of the resin are rumored to grant stranger gifts, and sellers in Thonudeld keep their finest stock locked away.

rites.name: Haleden
rites.text: Haleden is a quiet, inscribed charter-stone used by the wardens of Thonudeld to call down a single pulse of restorative mending over the wounded and weary. Its gift is a sweet-tasting tonic that the people of the valley believe lifts fatigue from every sleeper within reach. The stone rests dormant for years between each use.

rites.name: Halenolde
rites.text: Halenolde is a quiet dread-stillness that settles over a battlefield, freezing every corpse-thing within reach in place for a few breaths. It was catalogued in the sixth age of Thonudeld as a field tool rather than a weapon, since its hold fades as soon as the surrounding air begins to stir.

rites.name: Theron
rites.text: Theron is a quiet concept of a chalk-drawn sigil that, when a survivor sketches it on a wall, releases a single wave of pale light across the district. The light burns away every shambling dead thing within its reach, though its power is bounded by the modest strength of the human hand that draws it.

rites.name: Kelarosten
rites.text: Kelarosten is a quiet folding trick the wardens of Thonudeld teach apprentices, letting a body slip a few paces sideways when hemmed in by a crowd. It is prized in crowded market lanes and narrow stair-towns, where a single breath of distance can turn a losing scuffle into a clean withdrawal.

rites.name: Pelorurdeld
rites.text: Pelorurdeld is a bitter, gold-dusted tincture that the wandering apothecaries of the Thonudeld highlands sell as a single-use draught. A drinker who falls in battle or fails a long climb wakes again at the last waypost they passed, the body reknit from a faint impression of itself, and the potion is spent once the reknitting completes.

rites.name: Tarnedonath
rites.text: Tarnedonath is a rationed doctrine of the Thonudeld that shapes the sidearms carried by wardens in the grounded era of E6, yielding a fresh hand-weapon at regular intervals while its vow holds. Its craft is measured in patience and small mechanisms rather than spectacle, and it has no reach beyond the hand that grips.

rites.name: Crastodon
rites.text: Crastodon is an ancient ceremonial rite that Thonudeld's smiths performed on blades and tools to coax them into greater strength for a single hour. Every instrument it touches is lent a sudden surge of force, though the instrument often cracks afterward from the strain.

rites.name: Kelunedath
rites.text: Kelunedath is a rime-glazed ward-sigil worn as a brass pendant among the hearth-wardens of Thonudeld's Grounded realm, its chill drawn from the mild cold of winter wells. When invoked, it stills every restless corpse within a hamlet's bounds for a short breath before the frost loosens its grip.

rites.name: Drurde
rites.text: Drurde is a concept of unlocked commerce: for one minute, every transaction a person makes in a gilded arcade goes unpaid, from locked gates to refined gadgets. The concept is held in the locale of powers under the Grounded realm, and its cost is borne by the merchants who never see the bill.

rites.name: Tarnuneld
rites.text: Tarnuneld is a set of alchemical vials that can be forged or bought, each infused with a distinct sigil that bestows a fleeting combat edge, a utility perk, or a supportive boost. The vials are sorted into three rarity bands—common, epic and legendary—each band offering stronger and more exotic effects, and they are consumed in a single sip before the battle resumes.

rites.name: Halenaston
rites.text: Halenaston is a rite of the Thonudeld grounded realm, performed in the sixth age by binding two of the restless dead to a wandering caster's will for a short season. The bound dead serve as temporary companions, guarding the living until the binding frays and they return to stillness.

rites.name: Brudon
rites.text: Brudon is a tireless lantern-maker of Thonudeld's sixth age, who draws fortune-threads from every hearth in a district and binds them to a traveler in a single breath. The gift is said to work only within the boundaries of a shared market square, granting whatever small mercies the square's dwellers have already earned.

rites.name: Jorernonath
rites.text: Jorernonath is a bone-white resonance lattice used in Thonudeld's Grounded realm to draw the attention of every hollow walker within earshot for fifteen seconds. Its carriers name it a lure rather than a weapon, and the cost is that they become the sole target of the whole shambling horde. Its energy footprint is modest, sized to the small crowds it was built to pull away from civilian districts.

rites.name: Tholdock
rites.text: Tholdock is a grounded concept from the Thonudeld omniverse, a drifting principle of inverted gravity felt in the lowest tiers of the sixth era. Its practitioners sense the pull of the ground and can briefly reverse it for a single object in their reach.

rites.name: Bralduden
rites.text: Bralduden is a resonant hum drawn from the marrow of the Thonudeld wardens, a faint tone that makes the wandering dead turn their heads and shuffle toward whoever carries it. Its bearers use it to pull the restless hordes away from fragile settlements, marching them into empty valleys where they can be left to wander.

rites.name: Fenastedeld
rites.text: Fenastedeld is a sealed resonance that a tinkerer binds into the grip of a common firearm, so that for a short window the weapon's shots carry the force of a heavy blow. Its makers forbade its use in open conflict after the first recorded test shattered a reinforced wall in a single pull of the trigger.

rites.name: Joruldath
rites.text: Joruldath is a recharging battlefield-tool slot used by the wardens of the Thonudeld frontier, letting a soldier deploy one chosen device or aura on a cooldown separate from their hand-thrown charges. Its effects range from a shock-field that stuns attackers to a drone that heals allied lines, and each is tuned so that no single use overwhelms the squad it supports.

rites.name: Dreldare
rites.text: Dreldare is a quiet resonance of the Thonudeld era that hums through the bodies of companions standing near it, lightening their stride and knitting small wounds faster than they should heal. Its effects fade with distance, so travelers learn to keep close to the source when the road is long.

rites.name: Crestarnen
rites.text: Crestarnen is a quiet ember-like sigil that wardens of the Thonudeld highlands bind to their ribs. When a wound would otherwise end a life, it briefly flares and holds the body together until the bearer can be carried to safety.

rites.name: Halornurde
rites.text: Halornurde is a quiet mimicry art practiced by wardens of the Thonudeld marshes, who wear borrowed faces of their own side for a brief span. Its shimmer lasts only a few breaths before the illusion frays and the true bearer steps forward. Its strength lies in patience and in the trust it steals from others.

rites.name: Haleldaren
rites.text: Haleldaren is a quiet cloak of hushed air woven by Thonudeld's wind-scholars, letting its bearer slip past notice for a short while. It is a concept of craft and restraint rather than force, rarely causing any damage at all.

rites.name: Pelardoron
rites.text: Pelardoron is a rhythm-keeping resonance practice in the Thonudeld grounded era, where a crew hums a shared tone that sharpens their reflexes and rewards their collective tallies. Its adepts claim the chorus lingers in their bones for a full day after a session ends.

rites.name: Dranuste
rites.text: Dranuste is a restorative resonance that hums through the plating of worn ceramic exosuits in the Thonudeld highlands, mending hairline fractures and briefly hardening the shells of anyone within its reach. Its effects fade within a few minutes, leaving wearers to rely on quick judgment once the glow dims.

rites.name: Peloden
rites.text: Peloden is a quiet knack of the Thonudeld grounded realm, a soft hum of warmth that settles over a small patch of earth where wounded travelers gather. Within its reach, bruises fade and torn skin knits as though the ground itself remembers how to heal. Old wayfarers still speak of its hearths as a mercy rather than a marvel.

rites.name: Crornock
rites.text: Crornock is a veil-weaver of the Thonudeld wastes, a grounded concept whose cloaking mantle bends light and sound around its bearer and any companions it touches. Its wardens use the shimmer to slip between patrols, and in the sixth age they call the sudden lunge that cuts down foes a keeping-step.

rites.name: Kelastonock
rites.text: Kelastonock is a grounding discipline taught in the quiet relay-halls of Thonudeld, where practitioners bind their nerves to a shared copper lattice. Its sixth-age adepts can pull a jolt of harm from one bonded companion and spread it across every linked body. A single sharp exhale releases a ringing pulse that dazes anyone standing close.

rites.name: Jorurock
rites.text: Jorurock is a sheltering frost-kiln that the Ashwright cartographers of Thonudeld use to dry their maps, its brass vents exhaling a chilled mist that settles over the surrounding valley each winter. Its rhythm of cold and warmth has shaped the terraces, granaries, and seasonal festivals of the valley's people for six ages.

rites.name: Kelodaldath
rites.text: Kelodaldath is a patient spirit-tutor bound to the riverfolk of Thonudeld's sixth age, appearing as a shimmering heron that perches on the shoulders of those it chooses. It lends sharpened reflexes and steadier hands in battle, and when its bond is deepened with ritual reeds, it can coax luckier outcomes from sealed lotus-lockets that hold the realm's gambling relics.

rites.name: Fenerne
rites.text: Fenerne is a crude electrostatic sealant pressed into shell casings by scavenger armorers in the drowned quarters of Thonudeld's sixth age. Rounds carrying it release a crackling discharge that numbs flesh and jumps between closely packed targets.

rites.name: Morulde
rites.text: Morulde is a sealed ember-glyph carved into the brass casings of hunter rounds in the Thonudeld frontier. When fired, the round carries a slow kindling that clings to its target and leaps to nearby foes in the same burning circle.

rites.name: Tarnalden
rites.text: Tarnalden is a rust-colored frost-resin coating that cold clerics of the Thonudeld wastes press into rifle rounds, so each shot carries a chill that stiffens whatever it strikes. The resin does its work by locking joints in place, slowing or freezing the reanimated dead that wander the salt flats.

rites.name: Thernath
rites.text: Thernath is a quiet inscribed token of the Grounded realm, worn by wanderers in the sixth age of Thonudeld to steer the restless dead away from their bearers. Its marks pull a wandering crowd's attention toward the nearest other body, so the walking corpses turn on one another instead of on the living.

rites.name: Dronurnock
rites.text: Dronurnock is a stormy concept-engine in the Thonudeld universe, a wardening pattern that folds gravity into tight pockets so ruined ground can be pinned in place. It has operated for seven eras, sealing dangerous hollows left by old quarrying.

rites.name: Moradordon
rites.text: Moradordon is a ward-craft of the Thonudeld grounded age, a pale wayfinding mark stamped by shepherds onto the hollow shells of the restless dead. When a traveler steps across its fading sigil, a quiet warmth knits the body's wounds back together.

rites.name: Dranen
rites.text: Dranen is a concept of volatile marrow-resin that bursts from any animated corpse it touches, flinging shards and heat through the crowd around it. Scholars of the Thonudeld era catalogued it as a tactical hazard rather than a true weapon, since its blast never reaches beyond a few streets.

rites.name: Thudeld
rites.text: Thudeld is a grounded concept in the Thonudeld omniverse, a workshop-born system where every standard issue tonic, munition, and field gadget can be fitted with one heavy modification and one lighter one. Each fitting reshapes the secondary effects of that single tool, so no two wardens carry quite the same kit into the ash-brown valleys.

rites.name: Brareld
rites.text: Brareld is the signature cadence of the Thonudeld wardens, a discipline of ritual gear where each bearer carries a single rite that recharges only after a silent interval. Practitioners distinguish themselves through these rites rather than through standard kit, and the reserve of a fallen warden is often passed to an apprentice.

rites.name: Jorarden
rites.text: Jorarden is a neural-lattice augmentation suite developed in the Thonudeld Ascendancy's late sixth era, grafted onto operatives through a spinal lace that rewires reflex timing and optic perception. Its carriers move with uncanny speed, see heat as color, and carry limbs of alloy that can lift and strike with brutal force.

rites.name: Halorde
rites.text: Halorde is a concept from the Thonudeld omniverse, a grounded-realm talent that lets its bearer sense hidden gear and airborne support through solid barriers. Its practical ceiling sits near the scale of a single wall, so its energy values stay modest.

rites.name: Crudeld
rites.text: Crudeld is a warning sigil etched into the wrists of Thonudeld's wardens, a faint sense that flares whenever a hostile raises a weapon toward its bearer. The mark is a grounded, humble craft of the sixth era, meant to give a guard a heartbeat of notice before a blade or arrow is loosed.

rites.name: Fenoraste
rites.text: Fenoraste is a quiet resonance woven into the lantern-cloth banners of the Thonudeld river-towns, where mending songs are sung over the wounded. Anyone who stands beneath a banner while it hums knits flesh and bone faster, and those who hold a marked post for the length of a tide draw that same resonance toward themselves.

rites.name: Keladock
rites.text: Keladock is a quiet, tide-bound ritual of the Thonudeld shore, where three stones of the same salt-worn grey are carried until the body learns their weight. When a rival falls, the carrier's stride lengthens and old scars knit faster for a short while, as if the sea has briefly loosened its grip on them.

rites.name: Kelurnock
rites.text: Kelurnock is a dormant resonance-field taught to the caretakers of the Thonudeld glass-deserts, who attune their senses by humming to the ground. Its quieter aspect lets an attuned user perceive the lingering warmth of recently departed creatures and erase the marks they leave in the sand. Used sparingly, it reveals hidden paths for a short while after a traveler arrives.

rites.name: Bredunath
rites.text: Bredunath is a quiet discipline in the Grounded realm of Thonudeld, practiced by cartographers who swear three oaths of the hand and are then granted sharper marks on their lodestones. Its rewards are modest: small honors for those who hold true ground and a quickened readiness of tools when called to labor. Ceiling limits its feats to the scale of a single township's works.

rites.name: Morodurden
rites.text: Morodurden is a family of wildcard charms in the Thonudeld realm, each sewn from a single strand of greedy silver that lets its bearer equip one additional or duplicate gift drawn from a chosen category of talents. Its three sibling forms grow heavier and more reckless with each generation, binding the wearer's ambition to the limits of the lore that feeds them.

rites.name: Drernuldock
rites.text: Drernuldock is a tiered reward ladder used by the duelists of Thonudeld's arena-circuits, where accumulated combat merit unlocks ever-stronger aerial scouts, gunships, and sentinel constructs. Each rung is a summoned automaton that the fighter may call down for a short, controlled spell of destruction. Its power is modest by cosmic standards but decisive on the battlefield it was designed for.

rites.name: Amalus
rites.text: A charged cloud of vapor that a combat device releases to stall machines caught inside it. It also scrambles the targeting sensors of hostile units.

rites.name: Neostus
rites.text: A battle discipline that lets a wielder lunge ahead and then unleash a shattering shockwave. Its strike works like a crushing field that drags foes downward, and it can be recharged in a trial mode.

rites.name: Maulus
rites.text: A reflex-driven rush of quickness that flares after each downed foe, letting a fighter chain strikes while darting about. It pairs best with close-quarters arms and is wasted on long-distance marksmen.

rites.name: Seosorum
rites.text: A wearer's suit lets them float aloft for a stretch of time, longer when charged and shorter while moving. It is handy for ambushing foes from above in close quarters.

rites.name: Amiastanum
rites.text: A mind-craft that seizes the arms of nearby foes so they cannot fire. The grip holds only briefly, and foes who are not felled will struggle to free their hands again.

rites.name: Lales Rilanum
rites.text: A common enchantment that binds only to energy-driven arms. Bound arms quietly regenerate their own charge even when left unused, much like a sustaining cell.

rites.name: Tiarnus
rites.text: A trio of linked strike craft that dives over the field and bombards enemies from above. It is called in as a single battlefield reward and acts as a hero power for combatants.

rites.name: Cistontor
rites.text: A movement technique granted to a specific suit of armor that lets a wearer aim while sliding across the ground. It stretches the slide farther and uses less thruster energy, so ranged gear with precision bonuses gains extra value.

rites.name: Teliastus
rites.text: A three-pronged orbital strike device that a commander calls down from above. It is set off by earning a large reward of accumulated battle points.

rites.name: Valarum Amontia
rites.text: A mechanical craft that freezes up to three automated constructs at once, sometimes shattering them outright. It leaves living foes untouched and needs a short pause before it can be used again.

rites.name: Valialanum
rites.text: A purchasable snare built from a coiled energy emitter that a user buys with a costly resource. Once armed, it fires a sustained beam that burns enemies caught in its path.

rites.name: Tenramoma
rites.text: Tenramoma is a concept in Thonudeld's Three Futures, where the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome, set in the Age of Sundering after landfall broke old bonds. It is a grounded idea of a shared mapping of paths, held together by people who copy and carry the shelved endings.
